source.title: Social Information Is Integrated into Value and Confidence Judgments According to Its Reliability

confidence_rationale: Social information (online reviews) is integrated into BOTH value and confidence in a Bayesian, reliability-weighted way, and dorsomedial PFC tracks the size of the socially driven belief update. Integration into confidence is the collapse ARC-115 warns against, but it is reliability-gated and the update has its own neural signature, which suggests the social contribution stays separable at the computational level even after it is merged into the report. Coded mixed.
failure_signatures: Participants updated their confidence judgments using social information, i.e. socially supplied agreement does enter the human confidence readout rather than staying in a separate channel.

Because the integration is reliability-weighted and Bayes-consistent, a merged accumulator can be normatively correct when the social source is informative; ARC-115 must say why the separate channel is needed even when social evidence is reliable (e.g. to keep provenance for later discounting), or it risks forbidding rational updating.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Participants updated initial value and confidence judgments in a Bayesian fashion, taking account of both the uncertainty of their initial beliefs and the reliability of the social information; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex activity tracked the degree of belief update.
mapping.ree_translation: Relevant to ARC-115 in two ways. (1) The human confidence readout is not socially sealed, so the collapse is real. (2) The dmPFC update signal is a candidate neural analogue of a distinct social-agreement channel whose output is then combined, which is the architecture ARC-115 recommends: keep the social term separately represented, with its own provenance and reliability, before any combination.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Value judgments of consumer goods are not propositional belief or commit-readiness. The dmPFC signal tracks the update magnitude; that is not proof of a separate accumulator. Reliability-weighted integration is normatively rational, so the paper also questions how strict ARC-115's 'must not enter' should be.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults rating consumer goods before and after seeing online reviews of varying mean and dispersion; fMRI with Bayesian model-based analysis.

confidence_components.notes: Solid design and venue. Mapping moderate: value, not propositional confidence. The normative-rationality point is the most important thing it adds to ARC-115.
